title: pip & Virtual Environments
intro: Learn the basic ideas of pip & Virtual Environments in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: pip
items.text: pip is the common tool used to install and manage Python packages.

items.heading: Package
items.text: A package is reusable Python code distributed so other programs can install and use it.

items.heading: Virtual environment
items.text: A virtual environment creates an isolated Python environment for a project’s packages.

items.heading: Create venv
items.text: python -m venv .venv creates a virtual environment directory named .venv.

items.heading: Activate venv
items.text: Activation makes the environment’s Python and installed commands the active ones in many shells.

items.heading: pip install
items.text: pip install package downloads and installs the requested package into the active environment.

items.heading: requirements.txt
items.text: requirements.txt records project dependencies so the environment can be recreated more easily.

items.heading: Dependency isolation
items.text: Separate environments prevent packages for one project from interfering with another project.

items.heading: Version pinning
items.text: A pinned version such as package==1.2.3 records an exact release and can improve reproducibility.

items.heading: pip uninstall
items.text: pip uninstall removes an installed package from the active environment.

items.heading: Secrets
items.text: Passwords and API keys should be kept in secure configuration or environment variables rather than committed into source code.
